Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:65: And to be more precise about the matter, "He is God" may be understood through what my teacher, peace be upon him, explained concerning what Rashbi writes (Zohar, Beshalach 46a) about the "darkness of dawn" - and he explains that the intent is to include the measure of night within day and the measure of day within night. This is: by day, when it wishes to shine, there is darkness first, to indicate that although the measure of day comes, nevertheless the measure of night is also included with it; and when the sun comes, when it should immediately be night's darkness, instead the sun shines, to indicate that it is included within the measure of night - and this is "for the LORD, He is God" - that YHVH is Himself included within Elohim, and Elohim is YHVH, all one unity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:66: And what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Va'era 26b), in explaining this verse "and consider it in your heart" - that "levav" [heart, with the doubled letter] is right and left, the good inclination and the evil inclination - this is also connected with "and you shall know this day," whose explanation is that right and left are bound to day and night, right by day and left by night, as Rashbi explains (there, Shemot 18b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:67: With this a little of much that pertains to contemplation of the world is included. And let us proceed to explain the matter of contemplation of man in a chapter of its own:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:1: Concerning contemplation of the creation of man and his governance until the day of his death, and his good reward after his death, we have learned in tractate Avot (3:14): he used to say, beloved is man, for he was created in the image; but it was by a special love that it was made known to him that he was created in the image, as it is said (Genesis 9:6), "for in the image of God He made man." Already the superfluity of the Mishnah's language is evident: what does it add by saying "but it was by a special love that it was made known to him that he was created in the image" beyond what it already said, "beloved is man, for he was created"?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:2: And what appears to me in this is through what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Tikkunei Zohar 130b), and we copied his text in the Gate of Fear, chapter 9 - that man is called a microcosm, and all his limbs are arranged according to the orders of the work of creation. And in the Gate of Holiness we explained the particular limbs, each one by itself; see there. And in general, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Song of Songs [passage] (Zohar Chadash, Song of Songs 74a), in these words: "let us make man in our image, according to our likeness" (Genesis 1:26) - it is written (Psalms 37:23), "the steps of a man are established by the LORD, and He delights in his way." Come and see: when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the upper world and the lower world, everything was in one image, this corresponding to that. At the time the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to create man below, He wished to make him corresponding to the two worlds, and all the secrets of above and below are all within man - the skull of the head that rests upon the body is in the secret of the upper world, in those repairs of the head; the body is in the secret of the body, where the levels stand in known limbs beneath this head; the thighs and legs are all in the lower levels, as befits it to be corresponding to [above and] corresponding to below. And all the supernal and lower images the Holy One, blessed be He, engraved in man, that he be complete in everything - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:3: And in the Tikkunim (page 123a), another way is explained, in these words: these limbs are all in the sefirot - the head is Keter Elyon; the brain is Chochmah; Binah is the heart, and in it is "a heart that understands"; the two arms are Chesed and Gevurah; the body is the central pillar; the two legs are Netzach and Hod; the covenant [brit] is the "handmaid," the Shechinah, its sign - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:4: And in particular, one who studies the wisdom of truth [Kabbalah] discerns the work of the creation of man more than the other sages - as he studies in the Idra and knows the reason why the man has a beard and the woman does not have a beard, and other differences, and the matter of the 32 [teeth] and the tongue in the middle, and the three colors of the eye, and the form of the ear made in chambers, and the ten fingers of the hands - not eight and not six - and likewise the twenty-eight joints, and likewise the windpipe and esophagus - the windpipe having six rings, and the esophagus white inside and red [adom] outside, which hints at YHVH-Adonai; and his walking upright on his feet, not walking on the ground like an animal, because of his level being like the angels, who stand, as it is said (Isaiah 6:2), "seraphim stood above Him," and it is said (Zechariah 3:7), "and I will give you access among these who stand."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:5: And the matter of facial lines/features, which Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Zohar (Yitro, in the passage "and you shall discern," 76b) and in the Tikkunim (121a), certainly indicates the providence of the Holy One, blessed be He, over man, whom He created with supernal wisdom, as we bless, "who forms man with wisdom"; see there. And of this contemplation it says, "beloved is man, for he was created in the image" - meaning Atzilut, and all this within his body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:6: And even according to the plain sense, providence is here, as it is said (Psalms 94:9), "He who planted the ear, shall He not hear? He who formed the eye, shall He not see?" And the explanation of "He who planted the ear" is precise in using the term "planting" for the ear and "forming" for the eye - for the ear is in the likeness of a planted tree, which has roots below and a branch growing from it above; so the ear is made with supernal wisdom, for if the ear were created only to hear the word, it would have been fitting to have a single opening, without making the earlobe project outward below and the surrounding cartilage made in this shape we see - but rather it is certainly like the likeness of a planted tree, that according to the root, so the branch emerges: so, according to what is rooted in potential within the brain, that form must emerge outward and form the shape of the ear. And likewise for the other individual senses of man, for the senses are like the soul that is in the brain and are revealed outward in this form, for according to the root, so the branch emerges. And it says, "He who formed the eye" - because we see that the eye has a form of three colors, which, according to the plain sense, is unnecessary; and since the Holy One, blessed be He, formed it in this shape, "shall He not see" - this indicates His constant providence over man and over his particulars. And when you examine this in the way of the secret, you will find that the place of the planting of the ear and the shaping of the eye is in the attributes and functions of sight and hearing, dependent on the soul clothed within them - and understand this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:7: "But it was by a special love that it was made known to him that he was created in the image" - referring to the inward reality of the soul; and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (94b), that the soul is called "tzelem" [image]; in these words: Rabbi Elazar said, is it not that concerning the Shechinah it is not written "creation" but "emanation," and it should have said "and Adonai created man" - what is "Elohim"? Rather, the Shechinah is called "Elohim," and concerning that soul given to a person it is said, "and God [Elohim] created man in His image," meaning in the image of the Shechinah. And of that soul it is said (Psalms 39:7), "surely man walks about in a mere image [tzelem]" - for at the time the soul departs from a person, he can no longer move. He said to him: blessed is my son to the Ancient of Days! And my son, whoever blemishes this image is as though he diminishes the [divine] likeness, and the Shechinah does not rest there. And the secret of the matter is (Deuteronomy 31:17), "because my God is not among me, these evils have found me" - the evils found me because the Shechinah departed from me - to this point. Behold, it is explicit that the soul is called "tzelem."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:8: And with this the language of the Mishnah is made precise: when it comes to speak of the matter of the soul, which is a portion of Him, blessed be He, it says "but it was by a special love that it was made known to him" - meaning to him alone and not to the other creatures, even the angels; for of man it is said (Genesis 2:7), "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" - and we copied the discourse of the Idra explaining this verse in chapter 11 - and there is further support for this explanation in the Tikkunim. And there (page 116b) they explain a second interpretation concerning (Genesis 1:27), "and God created man in His image, in the image of God" - saying, "in His image" is the lower Shechinah, "in the image of God" is the supernal Shechinah - and along these lines it is also possible to explain the doubled language of the Mishnah, and it is understood.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:9: Further, it is possible to explain through what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Emor 104b), concerning "surely man walks about in a mere image" - see there - that this is another distinction besides the soul, which is like a garment for the soul, and from the "tzelem" comes the splendor of a person's face. And this is "beloved is man, for he was created in the image" - referring to this tzelem; "but it was by a special love," and so on, refers to the matter of the soul, as I explained - and this is the general manner for the aspect of the body and the aspect of the soul. Also, in the aspect of the parts of his soul, one finds within him nefesh, ruach, and neshamah of the level of Ofan, Chayah, and Kisei, as explained in the Tikkunim, and if he merits more, he is given ruach, nefesh, and neshamah of Atzilut - it follows that man encompasses all existing things, whether in the externality of his body or the inwardness of his soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:10: And therefore, when a person repairs his deeds and does not blemish them, it is necessary that the Holy One, blessed be He, be found with him - as it is said in the psalm "he who dwells in the secret place of the Most High" (Psalms 91:15), "for He shall deliver you... he shall call upon Me, and I will answer him; I am with him in distress." Behold, from these two aspects, the Holy One, blessed be He, is called Father to man, and man is His son - and it is possible that this is what the verse intends when it says (Deuteronomy 32:6), "is He not your Father, who acquired you" - from the side of the soul - "He made you and established you" - from the side of the body. And there is some support from the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory (Yalkut, Iyov, remez 914), as we copied in the Gate of Fear, chapter 3.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:11: And behold, from this aspect, a great love is aroused toward the Holy One, blessed be He, who formed him in His image, being found with him even though he is below, in Asiyah. And we will not speak of the wonders of the [divine] Name in the formation of the fetus in its mother's womb, and what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, elaborated, because this matter is mostly exposition, and whoever wishes to seek it will find it in the Yalkut (Yalkut Shmuel, section 83), on Hannah's verses, "and there is no Rock like our God" - and further in Vayikra Rabbah, Parashat Ki Tazria (14:9), and further in Job (10:12), on the verse "You have granted me life and kindness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:12: Further, why is the fluid of the eyes salty, and the fluid of the ears greasy, and why is the fluid of the nose foul, and why is the fluid of the mouth sweet - all this is explained in the Yalkut (Psalm 33, section 720), Psalm "sing, O righteous," on the verse "who lays up the depths in storehouses."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:13: Further, there is another distinction fitting for a person to discern concerning the matter of man's formation - what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say [expounding], "there is no Rock like our God" [as] "there is no Artist like our God" - that He created many faces among people, and no face resembles another. And the reason for this is that just as the souls differ at their source - for there are six hundred thousand holy souls, and their general categories are the face of a lion, the face of an ox, the face of an eagle, and the face of a man, and there are several distinctions within the lion, and likewise within the ox - so the faces differ below, and this is a wisdom, part of the wisdom of physiognomy, to know who is from the lion, and so on. In the Tikkunim (page 66b) it says: whoever bears the mark of the lion in his configuration is white in his face; whoever is in the configuration of the ox is red in his face; whoever is in the configuration of the eagle is green in his face; whoever is in the configuration of the likeness of man is black in his face, along the lines of the Torah, of which it is said (Song of Songs 1:5), "I am black, but comely" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:14: And of this category of contemplation is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say in Bereshit Rabbah (36:7) concerning Canaan, who emerged blackened - of whom it is said (Genesis 9:25), "cursed be Canaan," because Ham castrated his father, and Canaan told his two brothers outside; and they say there: Rabbi Huna said in the name of Rabbi Yosef: you prevented him from doing something that is done in darkness, therefore that man shall be ugly and blackened - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:15: And let us return to the exposition we are engaged in, and say that certainly, from the side of all the aforementioned aspects, it is fitting that the Holy One, blessed be He, be called "our Father, our King," and that we be children to Him - as it is said (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children of the LORD your God" - and this is what is said in the Mishnah (Avot 3:14), "beloved are Israel, for they are called children of the Omnipresent." And it is known that a person's love for his son is because he begot him, and especially if he is a firstborn son or a son of his old age; and the Holy One, blessed be He, out of His mercy toward us, chose us from among the seventy nations and called us His firstborn son, as we shall elaborate below on the matter of the Holy One, blessed be He's love for Israel. And without doubt, the creation of the first man was originally an act of will and free generosity, and because His way is to do good - just as the creation of the whole world was an act of will and free generosity, so that He would be recognized in His greatness - as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Bo 42b), that the essence of Atzilut was so that He be known. And since the Holy One, blessed be He, created him in His image, as we explained, just as a father gives his own likeness to his son, so, as it were, is the creation of the soul; and the creation of the body is a mold and pattern and garment for the soul, which is the cause and reason for the body, and the body is not the cause of the soul. And certainly His love, blessed be He, for man - to flow to him life, flow, blessing, and all good - is along these lines of a father loving his son, for every cause desires to flow into its effect - along the lines of what they say, of blessed memory (Pesachim 112a): more than the calf wishes to nurse, the cow wishes to give suck. Sometimes the cow, or the mother, is prevented from nursing her child, if he is ill and cannot nurse the milk; and so too sometimes the supernal flow is withheld from a person - not from His own side, blessed be He, for He always flows, like a father who loves his son, but rather from the side of the son, who lacks the preparation to receive; and when a person repairs himself, from the side of the soul, he becomes repaired and a fit vessel to receive the supernal light. It follows that the reality of this love exists from the top of the ladder to its bottom.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:16: And this matter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in Parashat Va'etchanan (267b), in the discourse we copied at the beginning of chapter 2, where he says, come and see, everything is called "love," and for the sake of love everything endures. And he says, "everything is called love" - that all of Atzilut is called "love," as explained in the discourse. And he says, "and for the sake of love everything endures" - that were it not for the love every cause has for its effect, to flow into it, the world would cease to exist, and the world would be found reverting to chaos and void - for all the levels are bound to one another, one to the next, from the top of the ladder to its bottom; and if it were to occur to one's mind that Keter would refrain from flowing into Chochmah, this would result in the destruction of the world, since Chochmah would have nothing with which to flow to Binah, and Binah to the extremities, and Malchut to Beriah. And to this it says, "for the yud, its tip above, is never separated from the yud, for love rests upon it" - he is precise in his language, not saying "for the yud is never separated from the tip above" - for this would be the desire of the effect to nurse from its cause, and this is a clear matter, that every effect needs its cause to flow to it in order for it to live, and therefore it is never separated from it and its love is with it. However, the novelty is that Keter, which is the tip of the yud - that this tip, which is Keter, does not need the yud - nevertheless it is not separated from the yud, which is Chochmah, in order to flow to it. And along these lines, "yud in heh are never separated, for in affection they cleave to one another"; and likewise "vav in heh - this is the bridegroom always with the bride, whose way is in affection" - and it does not say "heh in vav," to indicate the desire of the male to flow, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:17: And he returned and explained the bond of all of Atzilut: yud in heh, heh in vav, vav in heh - because he had only explained the bond of yud in heh, vav in heh; therefore he says that the vav is not bound with the final heh except because the first heh, which is the Imma, flows to the son, who is the vav, and binds with him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:18: And it says at the end of the discourse: "therefore everything is called love, and one is bound to the other in affection." These words appear, at first glance, entirely superfluous, since this was already said. Rather, it is possible to say, as we explained, that this reality of love is the bond of the cause with the effect from it, in order to flow, in the manner of a father to his son - if so, even from Malchut to Beriah, and all the levels of Beriah, this aspect applies rightly, to the end of all the levels. And to this he returns and says, "everything is called love, and one is bound to the other" - meaning, all the caused things bind to one another with a doubled bond: the love of the cause to flow into the effect, and the love of the effect to nurse from its cause.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:19: And it says, "and therefore whoever loves the King is thereby bound in that love, and therefore, 'and you shall love the LORD your God'" - the explanation is that the Name YHVH is called for the matter that He brings into being all the existing things in the world, and yet, nevertheless, He is not called "the God of the angels" or "the God of the celestial spheres," but rather "the God of Israel" - and this is "your God" [Elohecha] - that He is praised through you and wishes to be called "your God"; if so, just as He loves you, so it is fitting that you love Him. And how is it possible for Him to be related in such a way as to be called "your God," that His divinity, blessed be He, is bound with man? This is certainly through the soul, which is a portion of Him, given to man - through this He has a bond to bind His Shechinah and His divinity with us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:20: And through this the verse may be understood (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to the LORD your God are all alive today" - and the intent is that the verse comes to say how we are cleaved to Him, blessed be He: it says that we are still alive, and our life is through the soul, which is our own, which is from Him - through this we are cleaved to Him and He is cleaved to us. And the proof that He is cleaved to us is that the soul is in His hand to take at any moment, as it is written (Job 12:10), "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing," and as it is written (Daniel 5:23), "and the God in whose hand your breath is," and so on. And just as our eyes see many times how many healthy people die a sudden death - this certainly indicates His cleaving, blessed be He, to us through the soul, and therefore He removes it whenever He wishes.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:21: And concerning the aspect of the soul given to us, which is a portion of Him, blessed be He, the Holy One, blessed be He, is called our friend [rei'a], as the verse says (Proverbs 27:10), "your friend and your father's friend" - and He is called "friend" because three are partners in a person: his father, his mother, and the Holy One, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:22: And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Beshalach 55b) that of this it is said (Proverbs 17:17), "a friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity" - and they say, in these words: Rabbi Chizkiyah opened and said, concerning this verse, "a friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity" - "a friend loves at all times" - this is the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom it is written, "your friend and your father's friend, do not forsake." "And a brother is born for adversity" - at the time your enemies distress you, the Holy One, blessed be He, says what? (Psalms 122:8), "for the sake of my brothers and my friends, I will now say, peace be within you" - not "peace to you" but "within you" [bach], for Israel are called brothers and friends to the Holy One, blessed be He. What is "born"? Is he born now? Rather, at a time of distress, a brother is born in the world for you, to save you from all those who distress you. Rabbi Yehuda said: "born" means that the holy King is aroused with this strength to avenge you against the nation on that side, along the lines of (Exodus 15:2), "the LORD is my strength and song, and He has become my salvation" - to arouse mighty acts against the nations of the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:23: Rabbi Yesa opened and said: how much must a person love the Holy One, blessed be He - for the Holy One, blessed be He, has no service except love, and whoever loves Him and performs service in love, the Holy One, blessed be He, calls him "beloved." If so, how do we establish this verse, "your friend and your father's friend, do not forsake," and it is written (Proverbs 25:17), "let your foot rarely be in your friend's house"? Rather, the colleagues have established this verse (Chagigah 7a) as written concerning burnt-offerings. Now, "your friend and your father's friend, do not forsake" - to serve Him, to cleave to Him, and to perform His commandments - "do not forsake," certainly. And that which is said, "let your foot rarely be in your friend's house" - meaning, keep your inclination rare, that it not rage against you nor rule over you, and do not engage in another thought. "In your friend's house" - what is "your friend's house"? This is the holy soul that your friend brought into you and placed within you. And therefore the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, is to love Him in everything, as it is written, "and you shall love the LORD your God" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:24: And it is explained from this discourse how great is the Holy One, blessed be He's love for man, particularly for Israel, to the point that He, blessed be He, is called brother and friend to each and every one, and collectively, "for the sake of my brothers and my friends" - and therefore it is fitting that you love Him - and this is "a friend loves at all times," and likewise "your friend and your father's friend, do not forsake."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:25: And he explains the matter of forsaking through one of three things: to serve Him, and to cleave to Him, and to perform His commandments - it is possible to say that these correspond to nefesh, ruach, neshamah, whose secret is deed, speech, and thought, as we elaborated in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 3. And although they are not in this order in the discourse - "to serve Him... and to perform His commandments" - and it appears, at first glance, to be a doubling of the matter in different words, it appears rather that "to serve Him" refers to the service of prayer, which depends on speech, as the verse designates prayer with the term "service," as it is said (Deuteronomy 11:13), "and to serve Him with all your heart" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say, is there service in the heart? Rather, this is prayer. "And to cleave to Him" is the cleaving of thought, for there is no cleaving except through thought and the musing of the heart, as it says (Genesis 34:3), "and his soul cleaved," and the like, as explained above in the previous chapters. "And to perform His commandments" refers to the commandments that depend on deed, such as tzitzit, tefillin, charity, and the like.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:26: And corresponding to these three, he mentions in his warning, "let your foot rarely be in your friend's house" - keep your inclination rare, that it not rage against you - in deed, for the raging of the body through the inflaming of the inclination is certainly a deed, and included in this, if he inflames himself with anger, the soul and the Holy One, blessed be He, flee from him. "Nor rule over you" - in blemished speech, such as evil speech and idle words and the like. "And do not engage in another thought" - this is thought. And each of these three causes the Shechinah to depart from him, so that it finds no place to rest, for the fine spiritual thing rests only in a soul that is clean and pure of all dross. And see what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in Parashat Terumah (page 128a), which we copied in chapter 4 - that after several preparations he mentions for acquiring the holy spirit, he says: that a person walk on a straight path, not turning to the right or the left; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:27: And concerning these three distinctions, he is precise in his language at the end of the discourse: "and therefore the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, is to love Him in everything" - meaning, in all three aforementioned aspects, as it is written, "and you shall love the LORD your God" - and the intent is certainly toward the end of the verse, "with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might," which are themselves the three mentioned things. "With all your heart" is thought, for the heart is the root of musings and thoughts. "And with all your soul" is speech, as it is written (Genesis 2:7), "and man became a living soul," which is translated [in the Targum] as "and it became within man a speaking spirit." "And with all your might" is deed - namely, that with his wealth he performs charity and acts of loving-kindness through it, and several matters of deed that depend on wealth, for through wealth many of the commandments that depend on deed are fulfilled, such as tzitzit, tefillin, sukkah, lulav, and the like - for it is common for a person to perform and fulfill these commandments through his wealth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:28: And when a person discerns with his intellect what is said in these mentioned verses, he will see that these are matters close to reason - for it is known that two brothers are naturally inclined to love one another, because at a time of distress a brother will exert all his strength to save his brother and give over his soul for him. And behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, in this aspect, is a brother to us, to save us from several troubles, as mentioned in the discourse, "a brother will be for you, to save you." And likewise the love of friends for one another comes from their mutual assistance in worldly matters and matters of Torah, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 4:9), "two are better than one" - and when two friends, one senses that his fellow loves him from the heart, to the soul, he too will love him, and reveal to him the secrets of his heart, and will do him good in every way he can; and especially if the fellow already, beforehand, did good with his father and his father's father, so that his love is known to be genuine, from the heart, and not superficial - then this second friend is obligated to do good to that friend and perform his will.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:29: And all these aspects exist in the Holy One, blessed be He, who partners with man from his mother's womb until the day of his death, to save him from several illnesses, from several deaths, from several troubles, and He does good with him, preparing his sustenance and the like - as the author of Chovot HaLevavot elaborates (Gate of Contemplation, chapter 5) on the aspects of the Holy One, blessed be He's goodness to man. And just as He does good with him, so He did good with his father and his father's father - and this is "your friend and your father's friend" - that He is a faithful friend whose love is known - it is fitting that you not forsake Him, and likewise it is fitting that you not provoke Him, nor be ungrateful for His goodness. And to this he commands and says, "let your foot rarely be in your friend's house" - for your friend, who is the Holy One, blessed be He, has a house that He comes to dwell in with you - namely, His soul given within man's body; and if the soul is blemished through one of the three things mentioned - through evil musings, or through speaking evil speech and the like, or through transgressing one of the negative commandments - then the house is full of idols, and the King, who is spiritual and holy, flees from there, as they explain in the Tikkunim (3b), that He does not rest upon a blemished soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:30: And he is precise when he says, "and do not engage in another thought" - meaning, that one should not bring himself to improper thought, as it is written in the Gemara (Niddah 13b): whoever brings himself to improper thought is not brought within the partition of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Psalms 5:5), "evil shall not sojourn with You" - and it follows of itself, certainly, that the Holy One, blessed be He, will not rest in the dwelling-house of His soul in this world, in this body, since it is blemished.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:31: And the two mentioned verses - "your friend and your father's friend, do not forsake" and the verse "let your foot rarely be" - although at first glance their matter is one, that the intent is to warn against doing things that would cause the friend to flee from him, nevertheless the verse "your friend and your father's friend, do not forsake" concerns the aspect of "do" - as it is written, "do not forsake" for "to serve Him," and so on - and from the physical friend we understand the spiritual one, for it is known concerning two friends, one greater than the other, who did good with him, that if he comes to dwell in his house, reason dictates that he should provide him good lodging and clear the dwelling of everything repulsive, as it is said (Genesis 24:31), "come, blessed of the LORD; why do you stand outside? For I have cleared the house" - and if these conditions are lacking, that friend will distance himself from him. And to this King David, peace be upon him, said elsewhere (Psalms 34:15), "turn from evil and do good." And therefore, for the aspect of "do good," King Solomon, peace be upon him, says, "do not forsake doing good" - meaning "to serve Him," and so on - and from the negative you may infer the positive: the intent is to say, do not forsake Him so that He leave as He came, but rather hold onto Him so that He cleave to you; and with what do you hold onto Him? Through occupation with Torah and the commandments and the purity of thought - and, as it were, He is compelled to come dwell with you, since you hold onto Him firmly and make Him a fine bed and a fine, fragrant dwelling with several kinds of spices, and the friend finds contentment there and certainly will cleave there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:32: And to this King David, peace be upon him, alludes when he says (Psalms 101:2), "I will behave myself wisely in a perfect way - when will You come to me? I will walk within my house with a perfect heart" - and the intent is that he waits for the holy spirit that would rest upon him at midnight, when a northern wind would blow upon David's harp and play, and then he would awaken and the holy spirit would rest upon him, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Berachot 3b); and in order for the holy spirit to find a place to rest, he would make preparation beforehand - namely, "I will walk with a perfect heart" - and his saying "within my house" is to indicate the soul dwelling within his body, which is his house, along the lines of what we explained in the discourse, that "your friend's house" is the soul. And we already copied, in the Gate of Fear, chapter 11, the discourse from the Ra'aya Meheimna (Shoftim 275a), which explains that the stones of his house are his 248 limbs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:33: It follows that the essential dwelling of the Shechinah is only in the pure soul - and this is (Exodus 25:8), "and let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them" - it does not say "within it" but "among them," meaning within their inner being; and this is one aspect of the matter of the creation of man through the soul, which is a portion of God from above, and through it the Holy One, blessed be He, cleaves to man, to save him, and when he calls upon Him, He answers him, as it is written (Proverbs 17:17), "and a brother is born for adversity," and likewise (Psalms 91:15), "he shall call upon Me, and I will answer him; I am with him in distress, I will deliver him" - and this aspect applies to Israel more than to the nations.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:34: And when a person considers this matter, his soul will be inflamed with love, and he will say in his heart: am I, a mere son of man, formed from the matter of dust and ashes, worthy that the Holy One, blessed be He, whom the heavens of heavens cannot contain, wishes to dwell with me? And who am I, that the supernal King should come to dwell in my house? It is fitting that I make Him a fine dwelling, that He come to dwell with me - along the lines of what King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 101:2), "when will You come to me," and so on, as explained, [by] occupying himself with Torah. And when one who occupies himself with Torah knows what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Bereshit 50a), that Torah scholars, who abstain from their wives during the six weekdays to occupy themselves with Torah - the supernal union unites with them and does not separate from them, and so on - and this is the Shechinah - it is fitting that his heart be inflamed to love her as a man loves his beloved, and make her a fine dwelling in his heart, and so on, along the lines explained in the Tikkunim, whose text we copied in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 7 - so that the Shechinah find a place to rest, for she does not rest in a blemished place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:35: And it is possible to say that the Shechinah is called "your friend," along the lines we explained in chapter 4, that they explain, of blessed memory, that "and you shall love your neighbor as yourself" is also said concerning the female; and she is called "your friend" because she partners with those below always, to give them their provision, their food, and all their needs, and she is "your father's friend," who is the Holy One, blessed be He, for the governance of the world is through both of them together, as it is said (Psalms 89:15), "righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:36: And through this what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains on the verse (Proverbs 17:17), "a friend loves at all times," "and a brother" - this is the Holy One, blessed be He - is settled: both are designations for one attribute, [and yet] a distinction must be made between them. Indeed, along this way, that "friend" is the Shechinah, and she is called "the friend" with the definite article, it is settled nicely: "brother" corresponds to Tiferet, who is called "brother," and she "sister." It would also be possible to explain this concerning Binah, for the secret of "friends" [re'im] is Chochmah and Binah (Zohar, Vayikra 4a), and she is called "your friend" in relation to her spreading into the six extremities, and "your father's friend" in her union with Abba, forever inseparable. Indeed, the surface meaning of the discourse's language settles better on the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, as the discerning reader will see.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:37: The second distinction, concerning man's sustenance - our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say (Ta'anit 2a), in these words: Rabbi Yochanan said, three keys are in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, not given over to any agent, and these are: the key of rain, the key of childbirth, and the key of the resurrection of the dead. The key of rain, as it is written (Deuteronomy 28:12), "the LORD shall open for you His good treasury, the heaven, to give the rain of your land in its season." The key of childbirth, from where? As it is said (Genesis 30:22), "and God remembered Rachel," and so on, "and He opened her womb." The key of the resurrection of the dead, from where? (Ezekiel 37:13), "and you shall know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves." In the West [Land of Israel] they say, also the key of sustenance, as it is written (Psalms 145:16), "You open Your hand," and so on. And why does Rabbi Yochanan not count this one? He would say to you: rain is [itself] sustenance - to this point.
